sentences.text:
on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128065115/
1
Singh has fraudulently got his name entered in the consolidation proceedings.
On an objection filed by the informant, name of the petitioner was removed in the consolidation proceedings and again the name of the informant was entered.
To manage the property, the informant executed a general power of attorney in favour of one Balveer Singh.

The said Balveer Singh was looking after the said property, but in the year 2024 Balveer Singh did not pay him his share for the land in dispute and therefore, he had gone to his home on 25.02.2024 and came to know that he has expired
. He also came to know that on the said land, his son-in-law namely Mukhtar Singh had taken possession.
He found that it is the same Mukhtar Singh, who had earlier fraudulently got his name entered in the consolidation proceedings.

When the informant tried to vacate the land in dispute, the petitioner claimed that he has purchased the same and threatened the informant, thus the informant came to know that he has got sale deed fraudulently created and lodged the F.I.R.
4.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that sale deed was executed by the general power of attorney holder Balveer Singh in his favour way back in the year 1999.
Copy of the said sale deed is filed along with this writ petition.

5. Perusal of the sale deed shows that the valuation of the land even in the year 1999 was Rs.2,44,000/- while the same is purchased by the petitioner from his father-in-law (power of attorney holder) for an amount of Rs.1,50,000/- only.
There is no reason given in the entire sale deed for selling the land for much less than the market rate.
The sale deed does not show any bank transaction and shows notes acceptance of money by the general power of attorney holder in cash

,
therefore, there is also serious doubt with regard to payment of actual consideration.
It is surprising that there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner has ever his name mutated after execution of sale deed in the year 1999.
6. In the given circumstances, it cannot be said at the outright that the dispute is purely of civil nature as is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner.

Allegations are that father-in-law and son-in-law in collusion have fraudulently got the sale deed executed by using general power of attorney and also appears to have concealed the same for a long time.
Thus, prima facie a cognizable offence is made out from the above mentioned F.I.R. and no case for interference is made out.
7. In view of above, the writ petition is dismissed.
(Narendra Kumar Johari,J.) (Vivek Chaudhary,J.) Order Date :- 14.6.2024

Anupam S/-
